rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance potential. This experiment tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, which is critical for guiding subsequent experiments.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 52.7% accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly builds on the previous configuration while exploring a key design choice (fusion type) that could significantly impact multimodal effectiveness.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (a key design choice not yet tested) while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method consistent. It isolates the impact of profile setting and aggregation, which are critical factors with potential for performance gains.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018) achieve high accuracy (0.618). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) further improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. This is a focused exploration of a key design choice with potential to yield significant gains.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_025) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6287). This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer while using concat fusion, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing architecture with exploration of alternative aggregation strategies, which could improve performance further without overcomplicating the model.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l encoders achieve the highest accuracy (config_024: 0.628697). This experiment tests changing the fusion method from concat to weighted, isolating its impact on performance. It clarifies whether weighted fusion could improve upon the current top performer, balancing exploitation of the promising multimodal multiprofile setup with exploration of fusion strategies.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_025) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, isolating the effect of aggregation method. This is a logical extension of the promising direction identified by config_025, balancing exploitation of current high performers with exploration of aggregation method variations.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_025) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6352). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while keeping other parameters the same, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. This clarifies whether scvi_n200 could improve performance, balancing exploration of encoder variants with exploitation of the current top-performing setup.

The existing evidence shows config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.7062). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, to isolate the effect of aggregation method. It directly addresses whether transformer aggregation could further improve performance, leveraging the strong foundation of scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder, especially using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, achieve high validation accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) further improves performance while maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. It directly isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, which is a critical design choice with high potential impact.
